topic: The Ternary Bridge: From Hanoi Towers to Sierpinski Fractals
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Discrete Mathematics)

sections.title: The Hidden Base-3 Language (1 min)
lecture_lines: Towers of Hanoi map perfectly to base-three logic.
Each move transition corresponds to a ternary digit change.
Visualize disk positions as ternary numbers.
animations: Create 3 stacks of discs in the center (#FFD700).
Highlight bottom disc moving to adjacent stack (#FF4500).
Show middle disc shifting stack positions (#00FF00).

sections.title: Constrained Towers of Hanoi (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: Disks can only move between adjacent pegs.
This constraint forbids direct jumping across pegs.
Recursive movement follows a strict, path-limited graph.
animations: Display 3 rods with discs in Base-3 (#00FFFF).
Flash disc color to show movement restriction (#FF00FF).
Animate illegal moves fading away quickly (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Mapping to the Sierpinski Triangle (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: State-space maps to the Sierpinski Triangle.
Recursive fractal geometry emerges from restricted moves.
Triangles represent states; edges represent valid transitions.
animations: Draw large triangle with smaller central gap (#FFFFFF).
Subdivide top triangle into smaller fractal units (#FFD700).
Recursive fill showing depth-3 Sierpinski structure (#00FF00).

sections.title: Synthesis & Practical Application (1 min)
lecture_lines: Ternary logic optimizes recursive structure pathfinding.
Fractal patterns improve memory routing efficiency.
Non-binary architectures utilize this efficient geometry.
animations: Show data structure mapping to ternary logic (#FF4500).
Highlight conversion process between Hanoi and binary (#00FFFF).
Final visualization of efficient algorithm path (#FFFFFF).
